solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A letter said to have been used in acknowledgement

indicators.note: said tells us to take the word for a letter by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: A, E, I, O or U is a vowel, a kind of letter

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the single letter that was once used to signal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: A is taken as it stands; VOWEL said aloud gives the ending VOWAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open admission or declaration, so it is an acknowledgement of something.

clue.text: It is higher either side of this depressed area

definitions.text: It is higher either side of this depressed area

parts.words: It is higher either side of this depressed area
parts.note: describes low ground lying between hills or mountains on both sides; depressed is meant literally, sunk low

explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed area' sounds like an economically struggling region, but it is simply low-lying land with high ground on each flank.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley is a low stretch of land between hills, so the ground rises on either side of it.

clue.text: Draw these round dividing line

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch some figures in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of DRAW THESE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is a ridge separating river basins, and figuratively a turning point, so a dividing line.

clue.text: Illuminating cover-up

parts.note: a cover for something that gives light, not a revealing scandal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Illuminating cover-up' sounds like a revealing exposé of a scandal; read literally it is a cover for a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampshade is the fitting that covers a lit bulb and softens its glow.

clue.text: Fairly good way to rebuke

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: A reasonably kind method of telling someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning to scold is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate describes quality that is middling or average, neither poor nor excellent.

clue.text: Even soft wet earth cannot be seen at high tide

definitions.text: cannot be seen at high tide
definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the thing that is covered when the tide is in

parts.note: mud is soft wet earth
even means flat, level

explanation.surface: Level boggy ground disappears when the sea comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are placed in answer order, the earth first and the even surface after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudflat is a stretch of muddy coast exposed at low water and submerged when the sea rises.

clue.text: Edward brought up shy bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ed is the short form of Edward
coy means shy or bashful

explanation.surface: A timid bird is reared by a man named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' sounds like raising a child; in a down entry it turns ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoy is a model or tame bird used by hunters to lure wild ones.

clue.text: Some more belligerently resist authority

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people defy those in charge with increasing aggression.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against or defy those in power.

clue.text: Revised rate certain to produce wealth

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters of rate are reworked

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A changed interest rate is bound to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' applies only to the word rate; the synonym for certain is added unchanged after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a store of valuables or riches, so it is accumulated wealth.

clue.text: Inappropriate that first person will accompany Timothy, leading journalist

indicators.note: Tim leading the journalist means it comes before him

parts.note: I'll is I will, first person singular
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone joins Timothy, who is the top reporter, at an awkward moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of I'LL is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-timed happens at an unsuitable moment, so it is out of place.

clue.text: Can horseflies be caught in it?

definitions.text: Can horseflies be caught in it?

parts.words: Can horseflies be caught in it?
parts.note: a web traps flies, and a cob is a horse

explanation.walkthrough: Horseflies are real insects, but here the word splits as horse and flies: a cob is a sturdy horse, and flies are caught in a web.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobweb is a spider's net, which snares flying insects.

clue.text: Rubbish bride removed before first Saturday

indicators.note: before places the rearranged bride ahead of the Saturday letter
removed here means shifted out of place, so the letters are moved about
first takes the opening letter of Saturday

explanation.surface: A bride is taken away in time for the weekend's waste collection.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDE rearranged makes DEBRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or remains, so it is rubbish.

clue.text: Patriot melting alloy first

indicators.note: metal that melts loses its shape and can be recast, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A patriotic smith puts the alloy into the furnace before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLOY rearranged gives LOYAL; the digit 1 in 1ST doubles as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist is someone faithful to their country or crown, much like a patriot.

clue.text: A small hospital remains

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A little hospital is all that is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb; it is the noun, the residue of a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the powdery residue left after burning, including cremated human leftovers.

clue.text: Frank stirring rather hot tea

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is stirring his tea, which is rather hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it is the adjective meaning candid. The twelve letters of RATHER HOT TEA are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-to-heart talk is an open, intimate conversation, so heart-to-heart means candid and honest.

clue.text: Timely work quietly done on alternative melody

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
or introduces an alternative
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A musical piece played softly is performed to a different tune just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed or coming at a convenient moment.

clue.text: Used drill with old Penny

parts.note: an exercise is a drill or practice routine
D stood for a penny in pre-decimal British money (from Latin denarius)

explanation.surface: Someone called Penny, an older woman, did training drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name; with 'old' it is the pre-1971 British penny, written d.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to use it, so exercised means employed or put to use.

clue.text: Polished all over

definitions.meaning: first meaning: refined, with a finish applied
second meaning: completed, at an end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Polished all over' reads like a thorough shine; it is two separate senses of the one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished describes work given a final smooth coat and also something that has come to a close.

clue.text: Inn, central place of worship?

parts.note: middle means central
a temple is a place of worship

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pub might be the chief church in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inn' suggests a pub, but here it is one of London's four Inns of Court, the societies to which English barristers belong.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle Temple is one of the four Inns of Court, the professional associations for barristers in London.

clue.text: Want most of the resin

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter, leaving all but one

parts.note: want means lack

explanation.surface: Someone needs nearly all the resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lac is the sticky secretion of lac insects, the raw material of shellac, a natural resin.

clue.text: Furious fit of madness in terminus

indicators.note: in places the fit of madness inside the word for terminus

parts.note: a terminus is an end
rage is a fit of violent anger

explanation.surface: Someone throws a wild tantrum at the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminus' suggests a station, but it simply means END.
explanation.definitionFit: Enraged means made extremely angry, which is to be furious.

clue.text: Main trouble, American hostility

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of main are disturbed

parts.note: US, the United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: The chief difficulty is American enmity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' reads as a noun; it works as a verb, stirring MAIN into ANIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is ill will or animosity felt toward someone.

clue.text: I had backed minister, one on board

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so I'd is read in reverse

parts.note: I'd is short for I had
a rector is a parish minister in the church

explanation.surface: Someone once supported a churchman who sits on a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' sounds like supported; it reverses ID to DI. 'board' is a company's board, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is a member of a company's governing board.

clue.text: Actor's run without hitting the ball

definitions.meaning: first meaning; the 's stands for is
second meaning: in cricket, an ... is a run scored that did not come off the bat, such as a bye or wide

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs credited to the batting side without the batsman striking the ball, such as byes and wides.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a background performer in a film, and also a cricket run not scored off the bat.

clue.text: Ronald in court bringing up tips for waiters

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
in a down entry, bringing up reads the letters from the bottom, so the court abbreviation is turned

parts.note: Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: Ronald appears in court accused of pocketing the restaurant staff's gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing up' turns the court abbreviation round in this down entry, and 'in' sets Ronald's short name between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tronc is a pooled fund of gratuities shared out among restaurant staff.

clue.text: Engineers unable to withdraw

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
can't means unable to

explanation.surface: Engineers find they are unable to pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to retract a statement or belief, to take it back.

clue.text: Said to obtain nothing from poor area

indicators.note: Said tells us the answer is heard as these words spoken

parts.note: to get is to obtain; O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Getting nothing out of a deprived district, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a deprived, densely populated urban district, often occupied by a minority group.

clue.text: Horrible having become a bit taller, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: grew some: grew means became taller, some means a bit

explanation.surface: Something dreadful happened as somebody shot up in height.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means causing horror or disgust, ghastly.

clue.text: Lent moved forward

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... money, lent it as a loan
second meaning: went or brought ahead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' looks like the season before Easter; it is the past tense of lend, as in advancing a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to loan it, and to advance is also to progress onward.

clue.text: Senior withheld estimate that had been included

indicators.note: says the answer sits inside the words withheld estimate, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A senior figure kept back a calculation that had been part of a report.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest is the oldest of a group, so the most senior in age.
